title: Repertoire of the family band and Creole songs
summary: The family played jigs, self-made songs and many Creole songs, including the first singer of 'A La Ba'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What kind of music did your family band play? I mean, aside from being string music, what kind of pieces were they? Marches or Foxtrot? What did they have in those days? Well, I'll tell you.

Falses or what? Well, they had all kind of different numbers like jigs and so forth like that. You know, it wasn't as fast as it is now, you know? Then they'd have a lot of numbers that they'd make up their self. But I used to get an old man make up song, just with words. He'd make up his own words, this song. And sang them his self. Yeah. But now, well, a lot of this stuff they're putting on this rock and roll have been from the past. Some of them words have been from some of the old time they have sung.
Some of those old songs like blues type too? That's right.
That's right. All that come from back in them ages. That's right.
The things that your father and grandfather and all, were there any of them in French songs? Well, there's some, a lot of Creole songs.
A lot of Creole songs. It's like this number, A La Ba, well, Didi was the first one to ever sang that.

He was the first one that started that, A La Ba. So they could probably take any number they wanted in French. And all the people that understood French or Creole, you know, well, they would sing that and they would enjoy it. Yeah.
